subject.title: Manual context clearing for tool results

question: Should OpenClaw add caller-directed tool-result lifecycle control, and if so should it be destructive clear or recoverable archive?
rationale: Current code has only automatic pruning/truncation and whole-session compaction/reset/delete; adding manual per-result control creates a new core session/API contract with replay, storage, and recovery consequences.

options.title: Recoverable Archive Contract
options.body: Add one canonical core operation that removes selected tool results from active model context while preserving enough metadata/content for audit and recovery, then layer CLI/agent/tool-call affordances on top.

options.title: Destructive Clear Only
options.body: Expose a narrower delete-like operation that rewrites or masks selected tool results without recovery, accepting simpler implementation at higher workflow-state loss risk.

options.title: Defer To Automatic Pruning
options.body: Keep this open as a product backlog item but do not implement manual lifecycle control until automatic pruning and overflow recovery prove insufficient after related work lands.

recommendation.title: Recoverable Archive Contract
recommendation.body: Add one canonical core operation that removes selected tool results from active model context while preserving enough metadata/content for audit and recovery, then layer CLI/agent/tool-call affordances on top.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to cache-TTL pruning and the current moved implementation, and the decision crosses core session/runtime API boundaries.
